label: prospective numerical sensitivity; simulated; generic 2-D BETSE patch; not calibrated or fish-fin data
question: How does the simulated targeted and untargeted voltage response to a dimensionless Dm_K multiplier vary with the same gap-junction pathway open versus fully blocked?

model.system_dependency: ffmpeg, required only to render animation from saved trajectories
model.network_inputs: No external scientific data; install pinned Python wheels from PyPI and ffmpeg from the Ubuntu 24.04 package repository
model.world: 80 micrometre square hexagonal patch with BETSE default disorder; actual cell and membrane counts recorded from the generated state
model.world_policy: create one baseline world and initialization; copy that exact initialization and run config to every condition; BETSE seed is generated once for this packet and is not claimed to reproduce the earlier packet

intervention.quantity: BETSE change K mem multiplier on Dm_K for Spot-profile membrane
intervention.target_cells: BETSE Spot tissue profile in the single generated world
intervention.gap_block: BETSE block gap junction event, 100 percent, t=1..3 s

outputs: full per-cell Vm, membrane Vm, Na/K/anion/protein concentrations, gap-junction open fraction, coordinates and geometry for each condition
targeted and untargeted peak delta-Vm, timing, spread ratio, and end-window concentration deltas
animation of saved cell Vm states
limits: one generated world, one deterministic run per condition, no biological replicate
multipliers are chosen dimensionless perturbations and are not estimates of channel abundance or conductance
gap-junction surface fraction is not converted to siemens
no Kcnj13/Kir2.1 parameters, fin tissue mapping, growth mapping, measurements, or biological-success probability
a non-monotone response is preserved rather than rejected
